The idea of the `/v2/beacon/blocks/{block_id}` endpoint is that it is versioned both in the JSON response and in the HTTP header, allowing consumers to be able to decode it based on that metadata. Otherwise it requires clients to know in advance when hard forks occurred to call the correct endpoint for the block's ID. Not sure how the p2p part of it works, sorry. I should've probably started a thread, sorry 🙂 .. adding the responses here so it's bit clearer on the propose changes: existing `getHeader` response: ``` { "version": "capella", "data": { "parent_hash": "0xcf8e0d4e9587369b2301d0790347320302cc0943d5a1884560367e8208d920f2", "fee_recipient": "0xabcf8e0d4e9587369b2301d0790347320302cc09", "state_root": "0xcf8e0d4e9587369b2301d0790347320302cc0943d5a1884560367e8208d920f2", ... } } ``` new response with blobs ``` { "version": "eip4844", "data": { "execution_payload": { ... }, "blobs_sidecar": { ... } } } ``` Why wouldn't that be: ``` { "version": "eop4844", "data": { "header": { ... }, "blobs": { ... } } ``` The general form of all responses is to put the data in the `data` section. data is generally the actual object, and because the version string isnt part of the object, it's kept outside, otherwise its all kinds of messy so the `data` is the executionPayload object if its just returning that which is basically what <@144468805697929216> said heh sorry As long as `header` and `blobs` are spec objects (or there is a spec object that has both of these in it) then that format should be okay. (Otherwise we go back to creating objects specifically for decoding the responses, which then often requires shifting the data around between objects and gets ugly.) ah sorry good catch! the new response example is incorrect - yes, the proposed change matches what <@144468805697929216> was suggesting - so if data now becomes `"data": { "header": {}, "blobs": {} }` instead of `"data": {header object}` - would this require a version change? I'm new and not trying to break the existing patterns here - just trying to figure what it should be generally data is pretty much an ssz object... i'll try to read more on what you're looking at and see if i can say something less generic thank you! 🙏 im working from teh assumption you're talking about beacon-api etc so i'd like to make sure 🙂 oh this is builder api, PR here: https://github.com/ethereum/builder-specs/pull/61 I've updated the json example, thanks <@144468805697929216> This PR seems to be assuming that blobs are coming from relays. Is this correct? yes, thinking about this again, I'm not sure if this is necessary if the relays also publish the signed block and blobs (not sure if this is the current behaviour though) given this is all effectively coming from a spec object, i'd be putting it in the same spot as in the spec object for 4844 I can't find the blobs in this version of the spec https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/eip4844/beacon-chain.md#beaconblockbody the location in the spec will map where they go in the api... it's under fork choice https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/ed1c6be132e12850a50119f0f3815ca7cf8bb46c/specs/eip4844/fork-choice.md#blobssidecar Looking at https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/eip4844/beacon-chain.md there is no direct reference to the blobs, just the KZG commitments. So not sure why the blobs would need to be passed to the relay. if its going to map into the block, it needs to make its way to the beacon-chain spec and be in the block object, or we're deviating from spec, and that would be bad once it's there (on the bright side) you know exactly where its needed 🙂 it doesn't exactly map to the block though? it's ... akin to optimistic sync somewhat it's this additional side-condition which must pass (like EL validation) for a block to be valid, for gossip only. but it's not part of the block, and one can sync later with no reference to the sidecar I don't know how else the blobs make their way to the proposer beacon node, this is my understanding how the builder flow would work - please correct me if i'm wrong would it be possible for the local EL to request the blobs (that aren't included in a block yet) from its peers? i'm not really up on the design, i thought they were going to be part of the block but i haven't been paying close attention transactions in the block include blob versioned hashes, and the relays are providing us the tx root to sign over blobs are necessary to validate a block when they're referenced by the new blob tx type, so blob inclusion seems like it should be a responsibility of the builder right, but i think it should return blobs as well since a CL can do its own separate publish of the block (here with sidecar) like we do in lodestar i don't think EL will sync blobs ever, their processing just works off on commitments Correct, at least in the current specs, the only time the EL touches the blobs is when the transactions are in the mempool. So, if the EL gets a payload from its CL for a block via the route <@466006586477772831> described, inclusive of transactions, the EL may never have retrieved corresponding blob txns from other EL nodes while those txns were in the mempool

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content: The idea of the `/v2/beacon/blocks/{block_id}` endpoint is that it is versioned both in the JSON response and in the HTTP header, allowing consumers to be able to decode it based on that metadata.  Otherwise it requires clients to know in advance when hard forks occurred to call the correct endpoint for the block's ID.
